ratings.comment: Not every reading was the greatest, but super knowledgeable guy who does a great job of making this class interactive and engaging.

Prof. Emirbayer was boring, but this is also a classical sociological theory class so I'm not sure what else people were expecting. Definitely knew his stuff, wasn't the most engaging lecturer but I did learn things, grade is just attendance and weekly reading quizzes. Lectures were semi-discussion based which helped me stay awake.

Emirbayer was more a scholar than a professor. Lectures were very dry, tests were nit-picky, and it seemed as though he'd rather enjoy doing research than teaching. Textbook was alright as it presented material talked about in class; though at times, some of the arguments presented were a bit of a stretch.

Very awful professor, one of the worst class I have taken in Madison. This class for students who second language is English is very unkind. You can hardly catch the step of class even though you work very hard. He's lecture is also boring, basically reading book and no other interesting staff. Seems he is not paying attention on teaching.

Very good professor. As far as classic sociology goes, he knows his stuff and does a really good job with the class. The class is structured in a very unusual way, but I love it, and I think most people would. He's the best professor from whom to take Soc 475 in my opinion.
Terrible. He is like listening to static on the radio. Lectures were straight out of the book and were very boring and his dry, monotone voice made them worse.

Professor Emirbayer lectured directly from the textbook.  His lectures were extremely dry and boring, mainly because he did not seem at all interested in the class itself.  Exams were based directly from small details in the textbook so read carefully.  The book presented interesting material but unfortunately he did not in lecture.

I have a really mixed opinion of this course. On the one hand, I thought that the textbook was excellent and the material in general to be necessary knowledge on race in the US. On the other hand, Prof. Emirbayer (or as I took to calling him, Umirbayer) is a very boring lecturer, and I admit to starting an "um" count for him while bored in lecture.

I had very high hopes coming into this class, but Prof. Emirbayer made it almost a complete waste of time.  His lectures were dry and erratic, and the text book was unreadable.  I would not recommend this class to my worst enemy.

Material is interesting, but he is very boring. The class repeats the book almost exactly. they try to make you go to lecture, but u dont need to & they rlly cant notice if you don't show. Tests questions are very picky & are about specific details in book. Pay close attention to the reading & you should do fine. Overall boring, not too bad or hard

He was the most boring lecturer I have ever had. His lectures are exactly the same as his textbook so you don't have to go to class. The tests are very hard though. He has questions based on the smallest details. Information is interesting but there is a LOT of it.

Prof Emirbayer is definitely one of those guys who is an author first, professor second.  Lecture is essentially mandatory, which sucks because he just restates the book which he co-authored.  Read the text very carefully (best part of the course!), go to discussion, pay somewhat attention in lecture, and you should do well.  4 midterms, no final!

Very interesting class; it will change the way you think about race in America. Lectures were pretty boring, but he LOVES what he teaches. READ THE TEXTBOOK. Read it VERY carefully. If you are trying to get an A in the course you have to know the book. No final, no homework, no essays. 4- 50 multiple choice tests! :)
Very interesting and easy class.  Just go to class and do the readings.  Slides are posted, so just print them off.  Completely changed the way I think about race!! Highly recommended.
The information in this class is quite important

Be sure to read the textbook because even if he skips over the slides and says you're "not responsible" for that material, you are responsible for the text which basically reiterates what he says in lecture with more detail. He is horrible to listen to--terrible public speaker! a lot of ums and ahs-but the material is interesting. Overall, not bad.

Overall, I would say that the material covered in Soc 134 is very interesting and has definitely changed the way I view race.  The textbook is actually the best part of the course, so I would recommend reading it.  The tests are not hard if you actually read the textbook and take good notes. However,  the lectures can be boring at times...

Mustafa is very hard to listen to at times. He is brilliant sociologist but he is not the greatest lecturer (uses many uhs and ums)The material isn't hard and can be interesting but attending lecture isn't necessary to pass with a good grade in this class. Slides are posted online and they go right along with the book.
This class is super easy as long as you read the text book and go to class. The topic is really interesting but the lectures are pretty boring.

Easy class. If you go to lecture and read the textbook before each exam, it's an easy A. His lectures can be rather dry but he's very passionate in what he teachers. If you have an open-mind going into the class you'll enjoy it, if not, you won't. Highly recommend!

This class is very boring. Mustafa makes white people feel inferior and says um and uhhh like alot. He states his opinion and is very biased during class.  Read the book and youll be fine for the exams.
His lectures can be boring but he is a very nice guy. The class is not nearly as hard as anyone is saying. You learn to open up and hear other points of view.
Dropped the class. Class is very confusing and Mustafa's way of teaching is inconsistent. Not the best proffessor.

I heard horror stories about this professor and a lot of them are true. His lectures are SO boring and it irritated me so much when he wanted a discussion during lecture. I will admit that I did learn a lot in the class and ended up with a B so that wasn't too bad, but some of the exam questions are just ridiculous.

Cont'd: His book makes some interesting points but it's very biased. Many of his arguments are reaching and some of them are just completely inaccurate. He sometimes tries to engage students in lecture by asking questions and expecting responses, but most people don't want to talk in a lecture of 200+ people.

Prof Emirbayer acts as if the world revolves around him and his class. He gets upset if you leave early and doesn't allow laptops. He says he enjoys talking to students but said on the first day of lecture not to go to him with questions. He also doesn't bother coming to class during exams or when he shows a movie.
Mustafa obviously cares deeply about what he has to say, but what he has to say is misinformed and biased to say the least and at worst intellectually dishonest.

Mustafa is a real character to say the least.  He wrote the textbook, which is pretty awful and the same as lecture so you don't really need to go.  Exams are written by TAs so they are pretty poorly worded.  Get Charity for your TA if possible, she is intelligent and quite attractive.  Overall, it is a decent class but nothing special.

Mustafa may be a brilliant sociologist, but he is a poor teacher.  The way he conducts himself in the classroom makes it seem as though he has no interest in being there.  He makes no effort to get to know his students.  He is somewhat approachable, though, and is willing to talk with you if you press for it.

As interesting as this subject matter is, I really couldn't stand this class. The lectures were not well organized, he often got behind, and he could have articulated himself better. The exams (written by the TA's I might add) were extremely poorly written. He was not about helping students, and insisted that you ask only a TA for help.

Interesting topic, and he's very knowledgable, but he isn't a good teacher especially with underclassmen. Makes A LOT of references to his book, tests are tricky (they test whether or not if you understand the question rather than if you know the material), and goes quickly through the notes (power point). Likes to talk about pop culture.

I really wanted to like this class. However, I am extremely disappointed I wasted the opportunity to learn from this class from Emirbayer. He wrote the book, and is not only biased but obsessed with himself. Ok, Harvard, we get that youve done a lot of research but the fact that you cite yourself in your own book is ridiculous. Lecture also a joke.

This class was miserable to say the least. He is a terrible professor and his lectures are torturous. Half the exam questions were either written poorly, had multiple right answers or were so nit picky that studying became pointless. Take a different class to fulfill ethnic requirement

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! It is very petty. Prof Emirbayer is a hot mess in lecture. He is one of those people who knows a lot, but should not teach. He is constantly confused in lecture by technology, students, himself, his powerpoints-that being said, he is more in love with himself than anything else.

I'll say this as simply as possible.... he's a bad lecturer.  His first midterm was reasonable but this second one was ridiculous for the fact that every other question was nit picky.  I like to call him Prof. Ummmirbayer due to his 955 umms, errs, or ahhs within a power lecture.  I'd recommend a different Soc. 134 professor

The class is interesting, the textbook (which he cowrote) is interesting, and the course is moderately easy, but sitting through his lectures is painful. For his sake, somebody please teach him to use lights and computers, and let him know that it's not alright to say "uh" and "uhm" at a rate of 13 times per minute (I've counted) in a given lecutre

continued--his grader grades pretty fair and if you disagree, talk to mustafa and hell usually give you the point back...it may seem hard at first but itll ease up and youll most likely get an A or AB...warning: 2 hour lectures are super boring, but you don't need to pay attn as you will not be tested on the material again, and he may call on you

sometimes hes picky and would pick a random line fromt he text and ask you to explain...but other than that,his grader grades pretty fair and if you disagree, talk to mustafa and hell usually give you the point back...it may seem hard at first but itll ease up and youll most likely get an A or AB...warning: 2 hour lectures are super boring, but you

Previous comments are some whT accurate...if you could care less about classical theory and just need to get the requirement, then take him because its easy if you do ALL the readings and are able to find answers quickly in your text, as those quizzes/tests are open book...sometimes hes picky and would pick a random line fromt he text and ask you t

If classical sociological theory isn't an easy subject for you, then don't take this class with Mustafa- it will be hard! He tests you before discussing the material and could care less if you don't understand it. He has an insane grading scale, we had to get a 98% in the class to get an A. Discussions aren't bad. He likes to talk about pop culture

I think he has an innovative way of teaching the class; grades are based soley on non-cumulative quizzes each week and attendance. Basically, if you do the reading (THOROUGHLY- it's tough reading) and keep it fresh in your mind, you'll do well in his class. The rest is just discussion of the materials- just participate. Not too painful :-)

He is really a great professor!  He is both helpful and informative.  The pop culture references are a great chance to think about theory in new ways, or to stop thinking about theory if only for a moment.      I highly recommend this course and professor!

He's a little too zealous to teach classic soc theory, but he's generally easy to follow. The three hour lectures are murder, however--opt out of those. Also, he's a HUGE fan of pop culture. Interupt him at any time with an update on Nick and Jessica's divorce.
oh my god is this man ever boring.  you're not required to go to class but whatever you do, don't take a three hour lecture with him.  he's a nice guy, though.  kinda quirky.
